newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian stocks make modest gains at open.
newsitem.headline: Australian stocks make modest gains at open.

text.p: The Australian share market made modest gains at the opening on Thursday with most leaders firming a few cents.
The All Ordinaries index added 9.5 points to 2,736.6.

Bellwether BHP proved the exception among the majors and limited broader market gains, losing 27 cents or 1.5 percent to A$17.72 (US$13.11) amid executive moves and speculation of further change at its problem-plagued minerals division.

On Monday BHP, capitalised at about A$36 billion and accounting for nearly nine percent of the 325 company benchmark All Ordinaries index, announced the surprise departure of mineral division head, Dick Carter.
The company also flagged a cost blow-out at its hot briquetted iron (HBI) project in the Pilbara region of Western Australia.
"There is all sorts of guesswork about what is going to happen there," said a Sydney-based broker, echoing much of the talk about the results of the company's strategic review.
On the upside, fellow global miner Rio Tinto built on a strong London performance, adding 1.2 percent to A$21.05.
Elsewhere, Brambles Industries Ltd jumped to a record A$28.80 following the overnight release of results from by GKN Plc, its partner in the Chep pallet business in the U.S.
A narrow finish was seen the most likely prospect.
"I think we should finish up but there's not likely to be much in it," the broker said.
Rises outnumbered falls by a ratio of about nine to five, while about 38 percent of stocks traded remained steady.
